name: ASPIRe
aliases: Apical Suspension Repair for Vault Prolapse in a Three-Arm Randomized Trial
Apical Suspension Repair for Vaginal Vault Prolapse
question: Does sacrocolpopexy or transvaginal mesh lower composite treatment failure compared with transvaginal native-tissue suspension for vault prolapse after hysterectomy, and is vaginally placed mesh noninferior to sacrocolpopexy?

design.blinding: participants masked until surgery was completed; masked personnel performed examinations and adverse event assessments from the 6-week visit
design.population: Women aged 21 or older with symptomatic vaginal vault prolapse beyond the hymen after total hysterectomy; 376 randomized, 360 treated (arm sizes are treated participants).
design.description: Nine-center, three-arm, superiority and noninferiority randomized trial

verdictNote: Sacrocolpopexy beat native tissue; mesh was noninferior to sacrocolpopexy but missed adjusted superiority over native tissue.
takeaway: Among 360 operated women with symptomatic vault prolapse after hysterectomy, sacrocolpopexy had lower modeled 36-month composite failure than transvaginal native-tissue repair (28% versus 43%); Uphold LITE transvaginal mesh (29%) was noninferior to sacrocolpopexy but not superior to native-tissue repair after multiplicity adjustment.

reports.label: 36-month randomized report
reports.citation: Menefee SA, Richter HE, Myers D, et al. Apical suspension repair for vaginal vault prolapse: a randomized clinical trial. *JAMA Surg.* 2024;159(8):845-855. doi:10.1001/jamasurg.2024.1206
reports.followUp: Analysis when the last participant reached 36 months (July 2022); 296/360 (82%) completed follow-up

results.measure: Adjusted 36-month failure probability, sacrocolpopexy versus native-tissue repair (superiority, alpha 0.01, MITT-NTR population)
results.note: Composite of retreatment for prolapse (pessary or surgery), any POP-Q measure beyond the hymen, or any bothersome bulge on the PFDI question. 95% CIs for the failure probabilities were 20%-37% and 35%-53%. Interval-censored proportional hazards model with piecewise exponential hazards, adjusted for site and age category.

results.measure: Adjusted 36-month failure probability, transvaginal mesh versus sacrocolpopexy (noninferiority, margin HR 1.93, alpha 0.03, per-protocol population)
results.note: Upper one-sided 97% confidence limit 1.65, below the 1.93 margin (the margin corresponded to a 15-point difference in 2-year failure risk, 35% versus 20%). In the modified intention-to-treat population the 36-month probabilities were 29% with transvaginal mesh and 27% with sacrocolpopexy.

results.measure: Adjusted 36-month failure probability, transvaginal mesh versus native-tissue repair (superiority, alpha 0.01, MITT-NTR population)
results.note: Did not reach the adjusted alpha of 0.01. 95% CI for the mesh failure probability 21%-38%.

results.measure: Step-down superiority test, transvaginal mesh versus sacrocolpopexy (alpha 0.03, modified intention-to-treat)
results.note: Planned after noninferiority was shown; mesh was not superior to sacrocolpopexy.

results.measure: Supportive per-protocol analysis, transvaginal mesh versus native-tissue repair
results.note: Mesh met the superiority threshold in this supportive population only; the primary population did not.
Sacrocolpopexy denominator excludes the 2 participants switched intraoperatively to mesh (MITT-NTR population); it is 121 in the full modified intention-to-treat population.
P across the three arms. Failure was usually anatomic only (52%-63%) or symptomatic only (27%-39%).

results.measure: Much better or very much better at 3 years
Mean postoperative leading edge of prolapse through 36 months, cm
results.note: Sacrocolpopexy better supported than mesh (P=0.03) and native tissue (P<0.001). Total vaginal length was longer after sacrocolpopexy than native tissue (mean difference 1.1 cm, 95% CI 0.7-1.4) and mesh (1.3 cm, 95% CI 0.9-1.6).

harms.label: Vaginal mesh exposure related to the apical procedure
Suture exposure 12 weeks after surgery
harms.note: P=0.02. One participant each in the native-tissue and mesh arms required reoperation for vaginal exposure (suture and mesh, respectively).

harms.label: Return to the operating room during the initial hospitalization
harms.note: Occurred only in the transvaginal mesh arm.

harms.label: Visceral organ injury and intraoperative change in surgical management
harms.note: Visceral organ injuries occurred in 3%-5% per arm without a difference among arms; intraoperative events that changed management occurred in 2%-4% per arm.

harms.label: Modified Dindo grade III or higher events and serious adverse events
New or worsening dyspareunia
harms.note: 9%-11% per arm among sexually active participants, without a difference among arms.

harms.label: Deaths during follow-up
harms.note: Eight deaths in total; one cardiorespiratory arrest on postoperative day 16 was judged possibly related to the intervention, the other seven occurred on postoperative days 321 to 1802 and were judged unrelated.

delivery.label: Native-tissue repair performed

values.ntr: Sacrospinous ligament fixation 110/134 (82%); uterosacral ligament suspension 24/134 (18%)

delivery.note: Both required 2 permanent and 2 delayed absorbable monofilament sutures attached to the vagina.

delivery.label: Operative time and blood loss
delivery.value: Median operative time was 90 minutes shorter in the vaginal arms than with sacrocolpopexy; blood loss was similar among arms.

delivery.label: Concomitant repairs
delivery.value: More than three-quarters of vaginal operations included anterior colporrhaphy and two-thirds included posterior colporrhaphy or perineorrhaphy; full-length midurethral slings were permitted.

delivery.label: Intraoperative conversion to the other randomized approach

values.scp: 7/129 (5%): 5 to native tissue, 2 to mesh, for intra-abdominal adhesions
values.tvm: 5/121 (4%) to native tissue: vaginal adhesions 1, cystotomy 4

delivery.note: Two further participants were switched preoperatively (1 from sacrocolpopexy and 1 from mesh to native tissue).

delivery.label: Randomization after the FDA halt on transvaginal mesh kits
delivery.value: In April 2019 the 5 participants still awaiting mesh surgery were re-randomized 1:1 to sacrocolpopexy or native tissue.

delivery.label: Examination completeness during the COVID-19 pandemic
delivery.value: Physical examination was unavailable at 294/670 visits (44%) in 2020 and 181/622 visits (29%) in 2021; 301/360 participants (84%) completed a final-visit examination.

reports.label: Body image and sexual function
reports.citation: Andy UU, Nowak K, Menefee SA, et al. Body image and sexual function improve following prolapse repair. *Am J Obstet Gynecol.* 2025;233(3):182.e1-182.e12. doi:10.1016/j.ajog.2025.01.042

results.measure: Change in Body Image in Pelvic Organ Prolapse (BIPOP) score from baseline, 335 women
results.note: 123 native tissue, 107 sacrocolpopexy and 105 mesh. Improved by 6 months and stayed improved to 36 months in every arm, with no difference among arms in the change or in the proportion reaching the minimally important difference.

results.measure: Sexual activity across visits and association of BIPOP change with PISQ-IR change
results.note: 99/335 (30%) were sexually active at every visit and 131/335 (39%) at none. Among sexually active women, BIPOP and PISQ-IR changes were correlated at each visit, and the association persisted after adjustment for baseline sexual function, site, age, surgical arm and baseline dyspareunia.

reports.label: Frailty and mobility in women aged 65 or older
reports.citation: Erekson E, Menefee SA, Whitworth R, et al. Outcomes by frailty and mobility in older patients undergoing major urogynecologic surgery: a planned supplementary study of the apical suspension repair for vault prolapse in a three-arm randomized (ASPIRe) trial. *Am J Obstet Gynecol.* 2026;234(3):689-729. doi:10.1016/j.ajog.2025.11.002
reports.followUp: Geriatric and treatment outcomes assessed every 6 months for 36 up to 60 months

results.measure: Prefrail or frail (Robinson Frailty Index 2 or higher) versus nonfrail, adjusted hazard ratio
results.note: Nested cohort of 146 women aged 65 or older (50 native tissue, 47 sacrocolpopexy, 48 mesh). Compromised mobility was also associated with shorter time to failure.

results.measure: Prefrail or frail women living alone before surgery versus nonfrail women, changes in living arrangements for extra support immediately after surgery
results.note: 19% versus 6%. Other geriatric-specific outcomes did not differ between prefrail or frail and nonfrail women.

relations.note: ASPIRe's native-tissue arm allowed the two operations OPTIMAL compared: sacrospinous fixation (82% of the arm) or uterosacral suspension.
Also tested the Uphold mesh kit, with hysteropexy; ASPIRe cites its mesh-exposure rates for comparison.
